A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same i-LN research work. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v2 ends with references and has no appendix; v3 includes Appendices A–G and detailed configuration tables, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original restoration experiments, normalization comparisons, feature-statistics analyses, ablations, and low-precision inference results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–10.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds component ablations, regularization comparisons, repeated-seed analyses, and complex-degradation super-resolution results. The explicitly borrowed baseline scores in Table 6 do not negate the original results elsewhere.

M1.justification: v2 Equations 3–5 and v3 Equations 2–3 specify the same method: joint spatial-channel normalization followed by rescaling attention/FFN outputs using the preceding normalization's standard deviation. The new theory, backbone experiments, and ablation variants do not revise the proposed i-LN procedure.

E1.justification: The original training corpora, benchmark datasets, and four restoration tasks are retained. Appendix E.2 adds a complex synthetic degradation scenario for ×4 super-resolution, applying the Real-ESRGAN pipeline to DF2K training images and the same five SR test sets. This is a bounded extension of input conditions within the existing SR task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the original normalization comparator set. v3 adds LN with gradient clipping and LN with KL-divergence regularization as evaluated alternatives in Table 8, and compares SRFormer with LN versus i-LN in Table 7. These extend the comparisons without replacing the original comparison framework.

E3.justification: v3 introduces full-sized HAT experiments using 500K iterations for ×2 SR followed by 250K iterations of warm-start ×4 fine-tuning, an SRFormer configuration, and batch-size 2/4/8 tests. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The old HAT† results are retained under HAT2; newly disclosed settings for those existing experiments do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v3 completes the component ablation by adding LN plus rescaling without spatial holisticness (Table 3). It extends RPE analysis across ablation variants, shallow/deep layers, and training stages (Figure 12), and adds gradient-clipping/KLD analyses, seed-stability tests, batch-size sensitivity, and additional qualitative cases. These address questions beyond the retained v2 analyses.

E5.justification: v2 does not document a repeated-seed evaluation protocol. v3 introduces multi-seed training trajectories in Figure 11 and five individual seed results with averages in Table 9. This substantially expands repeatability and variability reporting, although formal confidence intervals and significance tests are not supplied.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the previously reported ablation and low-precision scores are retained. v3 adds rescaling-only, full-sized HAT, SRFormer, regularization, and complex-degradation results; Table 9 reports average Urban100 PSNR of 21.95 for LN versus 22.14 for i-LN under the new degradation protocol. Some normalization-specific Set5 results disappear from Table 1. Table 6 prints Set14 ×2 SSIM as 0.8276 for i-LN versus 0.9274 for LN while bolding i-LN.

T1.justification: v2 provides normalization equations and intuitive motivation without formal propositions or proofs. v3 adds definitions of inter-pixel structure and structure preservation, propositions concerning LN and holistic LN*, and derivations in Appendix G. The new analysis explicitly concerns normalization before the learned affine transformation.

C1.justification: The central diagnosis, two-component i-LN contribution, and claims about restoration quality, feature stability, and low-precision robustness remain. v3 explicitly extends the introduction's applicability claims to real-world IR and presents theoretical insights as an additional contribution in the abstract.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the mechanism discussion: it explains cumulative outlier growth through residual paths, connects normalization bypassing to equal-statistics degeneracy, interprets SRFormer's permutation as partially holistic normalization, and discusses why gradient clipping fails while KLD sacrifices reconstruction fidelity. These extend the original bypassing and bias-alignment interpretations.

D1.justification: Beyond v2's brief settings paragraphs, v3 supplies a model-variant inventory, detailed architecture and optimization tables, degradation implementations, channel-entropy pseudocode, computational costs, and a code-repository link. This substantially improves implementation disclosure. Some inconsistencies remain: Table 5 describes HAT2 training as 300K iterations, whereas Table 14 specifies 500K.

R1.justification: The original IR-transformer and abnormal-feature positioning largely remains. v3 adds references to Real-ESRGAN, SRFormer, BasicSR, and rate-distortion/VAE research supporting its new experiments and regularization discussion. It also adds a specific interpretation of SRFormer's normalization behavior, without broadly redefining the paper's research position.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially condensed and rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, observations become a standalone section, and experiments are reorganized into ablation and LN/i-LN property sections. Terminology changes from spatial consistency to spatial holisticness, and indexed backbone names clarify model variants.

P2.justification: The original Table 3 is split into separate ablation and quantization tables, Table 1 loses its Set5 columns, and existing plots and panels are rearranged or reformatted. v3 adds numerous experimental and configuration tables, entropy pseudocode, multi-run plots, expanded RPE displays, and qualitative comparison panels. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering or page-count growth.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens reproducibility and experimental support through detailed configurations, a complete component ablation, full-sized model tests, and repeated-seed and batch-size analyses. These address important gaps in v2 concerning component contributions, scaling, and training reliability while retaining its original benchmark results. The gains outweigh the added reporting problems, including the HAT2 training-duration conflict and Table 6 SSIM/bolding inconsistency. The expanded 'real-world' evidence remains entirely synthetic.
